record.title: Rethinking Diffusion Model for Multi-Contrast MRI Super-Resolution
record.reason: MRI super-resolution is the central problem throughout the abstract. The method targets detail preservation and distortion reduction in reconstructed MR images, with evaluation on public and clinical datasets.

record.title: Rotation-Agnostic Image Representation Learning for Digital Pathology
record.reason: The complete abstract concerns digital pathology representation learning and whole-slide analysis. Evaluation spans twelve histopathology datasets, including breast, liver, skin and colorectal tissue and named public pathology benchmarks.

record.title: Training Like a Medical Resident: Context-Prior Learning Toward Universal Medical Image Segmentation
record.reason: The primary objective is universal medical image segmentation. Hermes is evaluated on eleven datasets covering CT, PET and multiple MRI contrasts, with two additional datasets assessing downstream transfer and generalization.

record.title: Tumor Micro-environment Interactions Guided Graph Learning for Survival Analysis of Human Cancers from Whole-slide Pathological Images
record.reason: Human cancer prognosis from whole-slide pathology is the primary target. The graph model explicitly captures tumor-microenvironment interactions and is evaluated for survival prediction and explainability on three TCGA cancer cohorts.

record.title: Tyche: Stochastic In-Context Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
record.reason: The paper directly addresses medical segmentation and inter-annotator uncertainty. Its context-conditioned framework generates diverse candidate masks for previously unseen medical images and tasks without retraining.

record.title: Versatile Medical Image Segmentation Learned from Multi-Source Datasets via Model Self-Disambiguation
record.reason: The work targets deployable medical segmentation across acquisition equipment and protocols. Evaluation uses abdominal structure segmentation data from eight sources, with partial or sparse labels central to the training approach.

record.title: XFibrosis: Explicit Vessel-Fiber Modeling for Fibrosis Staging from Liver Pathology Images
record.reason: The primary clinical task is fibrosis staging from liver biopsy images in the context of NAFLD. Two datasets evaluate whether explicit vessel-fiber relationships improve staging accuracy and interpretability.

record.title: Spatial457: A Diagnostic Benchmark for 6D Spatial Reasoning of Large Mutimodal Models

record.title: SURGEON: Memory-Adaptive Fully Test-Time Adaptation via Dynamic Activation Sparsity
record.reason: SURGEON is a generic activation-pruning method for memory-efficient test-time adaptation, not a surgical application. Section 5.1 evaluates CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C and ImageNet-C classification plus Cityscapes-to-ACDC adverse-weather street-scene segmentation.

record.title: Test-Time Domain Generalization via Universe Learning: A Multi-Graph Matching Approach for Medical Image Segmentation
record.reason: Medical image segmentation and its morphological priors motivate the framework. The abstract reports evaluation on two medical segmentation benchmarks under both multi-source and single-source domain-generalization settings.

record.title: Unified Medical Lesion Segmentation via Self-referring Indicator
record.reason: The central problem is medical lesion segmentation across eight medical tasks. The method uses self-derived and external reference indicators, with experiments using four image-mask pairs and weak box or point reference annotations.

record.title: VILA-M3: Enhancing Vision-Language Models with Medical Expert Knowledge
record.reason: The proposed framework is explicitly a medical vision-language model. Specialized medical instruction tuning and consultation of clinical segmentation and classification experts are its main contribution and experimental focus.

record.title: VISTA3D: A Unified Segmentation Foundation Model For 3D Medical Imaging
record.reason: The work builds a dedicated foundation model for 3D medical imaging. Its primary evaluations concern automatic segmentation of 127 classes, interactive clinical annotation and zero-shot segmentation of new structures.

record.title: Beyond Euclidean Gossip: KL-Barycentric Consensus on Heterogeneous and Imbalanced Images
record.reason: Full research-focus review establishes general decentralized optimization under heterogeneity and imbalance, not medically primary research. Contributions and conclusion emphasize KL-consensus theory and generic optimizer design; CIFAR-100 is a main benchmark, with Kvasir-SEG as a substantial second application. Hospital motivation and topology/quality tests are acknowledged but do not establish primary medical focus.
